title: 1982 Paris–Dakar Rally
who: Won by Claude and Bernard Marreau (Renault 20) and Cyril Neveu (Honda)
summary: The 1982 edition of the Dakar Rally, in its African era: 18 stage towns and bivouacs through France, Algeria, Mali, Senegal. Winners — Cars: Claude and Bernard Marreau (Renault 20); Bikes: Cyril Neveu (Honda).

sources.label: The Drive: five of the most heroic Dakar-winning cars

approximate: Stage towns and bivouacs from Wikipedia's stage table. The rally ran off-road between them, so the lines are straight from bivouac to bivouac.

stops.text: The start of the fourth Paris–Dakar.

stops.name: Olivet
stops.text: Bivouac at the end of stage 1.

stops.name: Sète

stops.name: Ouled Djellal

stops.text: Stage 6: 568 km south to Tit in the Hoggar.

stops.name: Timiaouine
stops.text: Stage 7: 538 km to Timiaouine. Somewhere near the Malian border Mark Thatcher, son of the British prime minister, went missing for days with his Peugeot.

stops.name: Gao
stops.text: Stage 8: 740 km into Mali, then a rest day in Gao.

stops.name: Mopti
stops.text: Stage 9: 538 km along the Niger to Mopti.

stops.name: Gao
stops.text: Stage 10: back to Gao, and another rest day.

stops.name: Nioro du Sahel
stops.text: Stage 13: 517 km west to Nioro du Sahel.

stops.name: Dahra
stops.text: Stage 15 to Dahra, then on via Tiougoune.

stops.name: Dakar
stops.text: The finish. The Marreau brothers won the cars in their own Renault 20 Turbo 4x4, and Cyril Neveu the bikes for Honda, his third win.
